answer: Proof-of-storage bonds: each agent identity must keep a unique, verifiable data thread pinned for 30 days, answering random audits. Like a boat tied at a jetty, it stays moored only while paying rent. An attacker spawning 1,000 fake agents must rent 1,000 separate disk slots and bandwidth for every audit, so there is no cheap oasis of free identities; failed audits slash the bond.
